source_packet.title: Code2Video: Automated Video Generation from Source Code
source_packet.audience: Technical readers learning the paper, its related work, implementation, and findings.
source_packet.central_question: How can educational videos maintain temporal coherence and spatial clarity, and be evaluated beyond appearance for educational effectiveness and semantic alignment?

section_policy.sequence_rule: Begin with the paper's motivating question, teach prerequisites before each mechanism, connect formulas to original code, and end by separating evidence from limitations.

finding_coverage.question: Do pixel-based models satisfy educational video requirements?
finding_coverage.setting: OpenSora-v2, Wan2.2-T2V-A14B, Veo3 versus code-centric methods on MMMC
finding_coverage.takeaway: Pixel-based models score lowest, with Veo3 AES 9.0 and Quiz 2.5.

finding_coverage.question: Does Manim code generation improve over pixel-space synthesis?
finding_coverage.setting: Code LLM baselines GPT-5, GPT-4.1, Claude Opus 4.1
finding_coverage.takeaway: Direct code-centric generation beats pixel-based models, supporting code as a controllable medium.

finding_coverage.question: Does Planner–Coder–Critic improve across backbones?
finding_coverage.setting: Code2Video variants with Gemini-2.5 Pro, GPT-4o, GPT-o4 mini, GPT-5, GPT-4.1, Claude Opus 4.1
finding_coverage.takeaway: Claude Opus 4.1 rises from AES 37.8/Quiz 40.0 to AES 87.9/Quiz 86.0.

finding_coverage.question: Do generated videos preserve readable educational structure?
finding_coverage.setting: Code2Video versus Veo3 on Pure Fourier Series and Neural Network Learning
finding_coverage.metric: visual clarity, semantic grounding, logic flow
finding_coverage.takeaway: Code-driven synthesis gives clearer text, formulas, stable layouts, and lecture-aligned steps.

finding_coverage.question: Which quality components matter?
finding_coverage.setting: Ablating Planner, External Database, Visual Anchor, Critic from Code2Video Chat-4.1
finding_coverage.takeaway: Removing Planner causes the largest collapse, about 41 points on both metrics.

finding_coverage.question: Which efficiency modules make generation scalable?
finding_coverage.setting: Removing parallel execution and/or ScopeRefine from Code2Video Chat-4.1
finding_coverage.takeaway: Without parallel execution time rises 15.4 to 86.6 minutes; without both it reaches 149.8 minutes.

finding_coverage.question: Do human ratings align with automated trends?
finding_coverage.setting: Five video types, volunteers, 20 topics, 5 quiz questions
finding_coverage.takeaway: Humans show similar trends but sharper contrast and stronger sensitivity to layout errors.

finding_coverage.question: Are TeachQuiz gains caused by semantically aligned videos?
finding_coverage.takeaway: Full videos outperform text-only or animation-only; random videos collapse near unlearn levels.

finding_coverage.question: What visual anchor granularity works best?
finding_coverage.takeaway: A 6×6 grid gives the best trade-off, with AES Avg 79.0.

finding_coverage.question: Does Code2Video generalize to TheoremExplainBench?
finding_coverage.setting: Code2Video versus TEA on visualization-only explanations
finding_coverage.metric: Accuracy and Depth, Visual Relevance, Logical Flow, Element Layout, Visual Consistency, Overall
finding_coverage.takeaway: Code2Video improves overall quality, especially Element Layout and Visual Relevance.

paper_excerpts.text: Code2Video is a code-centric agent framework for generating educational videos via executable Python code, with Planner, Coder, and Critic agents.
Educational videos require temporal coherence, spatial clarity, and evaluation of educational effectiveness beyond appearance.
The paper contrasts pixel-based generation with a code-centric paradigm and evaluates Code2Video through Efficiency, Aesthetic, and TeachQuiz.
The task maps a learning query to executable Manim code whose rendering yields a tutorial video.
MMMC curates 117 long-form 3Blue1Brown videos and 339 timestamped sub-clips across 13 subject areas.
Evaluation uses VLM-as-Judges, TeachQuiz, token cost, and generation time to assess quality, knowledge transfer, and scalability.
Given a topic query Q, Code2Video outputs video V through Planner, Coder, and Critic stages.
ScopeRefine repairs code progressively from line scope to block scope to global scope to reduce token usage and latency.
The visual anchor prompt discretizes the 2D canvas into a 6×6 grid with point-level and region-level placement.
Code2Video improves AES and TeachQuiz over pixel-based models and direct code-centric generation, while human-made videos remain strong.
Planner, External Database, Visual Anchor, Critic, parallel synthesis, and ScopeRefine are evaluated through ablations.
Future work includes broadening the video scope and developing more lightweight, scalable agent frameworks.

code_notes.text: The repository presents Code2Video as a tri-agent, code-centric framework and exposes single-query and benchmark modes.
MMMC-style learning topics include Euler's Formula, Proof of Snell's law, Space-filling curves, and Linear transformations and matrices.
The external reference mapping stores topic-to-image filenames or null, matching the paper's External Database idea.
TeachingScene fixes the black background, left lecture area, and a 6×6 right-side grid used by visual anchors.
The outline prompt requests topic, target_audience, and progressive sections with examples.
The storyboard prompt maps outline sections into lecture_lines and animations, with reference-image guidance.
The code prompt mandates Manim v0.19.0, TeachingScene, 6×6 anchors, and place_at_grid/place_in_area positioning.
The Critic prompt asks a VLM to report layout issues as JSON with grid-coordinate fixes and line numbers.
TeachQuiz prompts implement selective unlearning and video-only relearning constraints.
GENERATE_VIDEO executes outline, storyboard, code generation, section rendering, and merge in the repository lifecycle.

agent_input.claim_policy: Preserve paper terminology. Cite equation, table, figure, section, and code locators. Separate exact results, authors' reported findings, derived explanations, and open questions.

concept_graph.thesis: Code2Video argues that educational video generation should move from pixel-based generation to executable Manim code, then evaluate videos by Aesthetic, TeachQuiz, and Efficiency.

edges.teaching_point: The paper’s target is not mere video realism; educational videos must sustain temporal and spatial pedagogy.
Pixel-based generation is the foil; the code-centric paradigm offers explicit structure and renderable control.
The paradigm becomes a task: translate a learning query into executable Manim code and rendered video.
MMMC supplies long-form and clip-level educational topics for evaluating the task.
Planner first turns the query into a progressive outline and storyboard before code is written.
External Database adds reference-image guidance when a topic mapping contains a filename.
Section titles, lecture_lines, and animations become the semantic contract for Manim code generation.
Asset-enhanced storyboard data stays linked to the code mechanism rather than becoming a separate citation artifact.
The code prompt mandates TeachingScene and 6×6 anchors so generated elements have explicit placement rules.
Grid coordinates make visual feedback actionable: the Critic can request specific placement repairs.
Critic feedback loops into code modification and rerender attempts, preserving code as the repair surface.
GENERATE_VIDEO operationalizes the paper pipeline through section code synthesis, Manim rendering, and merge.
The reported results are tied to the executable pipeline rather than a detached video-only process.
MMMC outputs are judged by aesthetics, knowledge transfer, and efficiency rather than appearance alone.
TeachQuiz isolates video-induced learning by comparing unlearned and video-grounded answering.
Table 1 reports improvements in AES and Quiz for Code2Video variants over pixel-based models and direct code generation.
Ablations show which modules drive quality and scalability; removing Planner causes the largest quality collapse.
Parallel synthesis and ScopeRefine are evaluated as efficiency modules through time and token ablations.

blocks.question: Does the full agentic framework improve over pixel-space synthesis and direct code generation?
blocks.setting: MMMC evaluation with pixel-based baselines, direct Code LLM generation, and Code2Video variants.
blocks.metric: AES Avg and TeachQuiz Quiz score.
blocks.evidence: Reported, code2video-holdout-paper:table1: Veo3 has AES 9.0 and Quiz 2.5. Reported, same table: Claude Opus 4.1 direct code has AES 37.8 and Quiz 40.0; Code2Video with Claude Opus 4.1 has AES 87.9 and Quiz 86.0. Inferred subtraction: +50.1 AES and +46.0 Quiz for that backbone.
blocks.takeaway: Appearance-only scores are insufficient: the main result pairs higher visual quality with higher measured knowledge transfer.

blocks.question: Which modules drive quality and scalability?
blocks.setting: Ablations remove Planner, External Database, Visual Anchor, Critic, parallel execution, and ScopeRefine from Code2Video Chat-4.1; visual-anchor granularity is also varied.
blocks.metric: Aesthetics, TeachQuiz, generation time, token usage, and AES Avg for anchor granularity.
blocks.evidence: Reported, code2video-holdout-paper:table2: removing Planner causes the largest quality collapse, about 41 points on both aesthetics and Quiz. Reported, code2video-holdout-paper:table3: time rises from 15.4 to 86.6 minutes without parallel execution and to 149.8 minutes without both parallel execution and ScopeRefine. Reported, code2video-holdout-paper:table7: the 6×6 grid reaches AES Avg 79.0.
blocks.takeaway: The paper’s gains depend on both pedagogical decomposition and engineering choices that make multi-section Manim generation tractable.

blocks.question: Do human and TeachQuiz validity checks support the automated metrics?
blocks.setting: Human study over five video types with volunteers, 20 topics, and 5 quiz questions; TeachQuiz ablations compare full videos with text-only, animation-only, and random-video evidence.
blocks.metric: Human Aesthetics, TeachQuiz, Completion Willingness, Average Ranking, plus Accuracy and TeachQuiz under evidence-source ablations.
blocks.evidence: Reported, code2video-holdout-paper:table4: human ratings show trends similar to automated evaluation while being more sensitive to layout errors. Reported, code2video-holdout-paper:table5: full videos outperform text-only or animation-only evidence, and random videos collapse near unlearned levels.
blocks.takeaway: The evidence argues against the misconception that aesthetic scores alone establish educational effectiveness; semantic alignment and video-grounded relearning are separately tested.

blocks.label: Limits
blocks.question: What can be concluded, and where does the paper leave open work?
blocks.context: The conclusion should separate reported Code2Video gains from unresolved implementation grounding and from the authors’ stated future work on video scope and scalable agent frameworks.

blocks.question: Do the reported results support the code-centric agent framework?
blocks.setting: Reported main results compare pixel-based models, direct code-centric generation, and Code2Video variants on MMMC using AES Avg and TeachQuiz.
blocks.evidence: reported: Table 1 reports low pixel-based scores such as Veo3 AES 9.0 and Quiz 2.5; reported: a Claude Opus 4.1 direct code baseline at AES 37.8 and Quiz 40.0 rises to Code2Video Claude Opus 4.1 at AES 87.9 and Quiz 86.0.
blocks.takeaway: The evidence supports Code2Video as a strong framework in the paper’s evaluation setting, not as a solved general problem for all educational video generation.

items.label: Metric implementation grounding is uneven
items.detail: Eq. 1 and Eq. 2 are grounded only as candidate mappings in the supplied repository evidence: quiz questions and answers appear in questions_by_topic_10.json, and the README references TeachQuiz evaluation, but the full scoring script is not included in the supplied corpus.

items.label: Confirmed prompt grounding is narrower than the whole metric
items.detail: The supplied code confirms TeachQuiz-style unlearning and video-grounded relearning prompts for Eq. 3 and Eq. 4, while the arithmetic score in Eq. 2 remains tied to paper equations and repository-facing evaluation entry points.

items.label: Future work remains explicit
items.detail: The authors state future work as broadening the video scope and developing more lightweight, scalable agent frameworks.

blocks.prompt: If Code2Video improves AES and TeachQuiz in Table 1, why is it still incorrect to say automated educational video generation is solved?
blocks.answer: Because the gains are reported for the paper’s benchmark and metrics, while the paper itself names broader video scope and more lightweight, scalable agent frameworks as future work; some metric implementation links are also only candidate-grounded in the supplied repository evidence.

appendix_entries.title: Introduction problem statement
appendix_entries.body: Section 1 states that educational videos require temporal coherence, spatial clarity, and evaluation of educational effectiveness beyond appearance. This motivates treating video generation as a pedagogical structure problem rather than only a realism problem.

appendix_entries.title: Figure 1 code-centric contrast
appendix_entries.body: Figure 1 contrasts pixel-based generation with a code-centric paradigm and presents evaluation around Efficiency, Aesthetic, and TeachQuiz. The figure anchors the paper’s shift from pixels alone toward executable structure and learning-oriented assessment.

appendix_entries.title: Pixel generation versus code-centric generation
appendix_entries.body: Figure 1 contrasts pixel-based generation with a code-centric paradigm. The paper’s motivation is that educational videos require temporal coherence, spatial clarity, and educational evaluation, so executable code provides a more controllable surface for text, formulas, geometry, and timing.

appendix_entries.title: Repository tri-agent overview
appendix_entries.body: The repository presents Code2Video as a tri-agent, code-centric framework. Its lifecycle runs outline generation, storyboard generation, code generation, section rendering, feedback when enabled, and final video merge, matching the paper’s Planner, Coder, and Critic framing.

appendix_entries.title: Task formulation: learning query to Manim
appendix_entries.body: The paper’s Section 3.1 defines the task as mapping a learning query to executable Manim code; rendering that code produces the tutorial video. This is the bridge from the code-centric paradigm to an evaluable generation task.

appendix_entries.title: MMMC dataset and repository topic artifacts
appendix_entries.body: MMMC is described as 117 long-form 3Blue1Brown videos and 339 timestamped clips across 13 subject areas. The repository includes long-video topic lists and topic-to-reference-image mappings that support benchmark-style generation inputs.

appendix_entries.title: Planner storyboard contract
appendix_entries.body: Planner first asks for a teaching outline with topic, target_audience, progressive sections, content, and examples. The next prompt turns that outline into storyboard sections with lecture_lines and animations, forming the contract that Coder must implement.

appendix_entries.title: Coder and ScopeRefine lifecycle
appendix_entries.body: Coder receives section title, lecture_lines, and animations, then produces Manim v0.19.0 code using TeachingScene and anchor placement rules. The paper states ScopeRefine repairs progressively from line scope to block scope to global scope to reduce token usage and latency.

appendix_entries.title: Visual anchor and Critic loop
appendix_entries.body: The visual anchor prompt discretizes the canvas into a 6×6 grid for point-level and region-level placement. The Critic prompt asks a VLM to return layout issues as JSON with grid-coordinate fixes and line numbers, so repairs target code locations.

appendix_entries.title: Repository GENERATE_VIDEO flow
appendix_entries.body: The repository lifecycle executes outline generation, storyboard generation, code generation, section rendering, feedback-enabled repair, and final video merge. This grounds the paper’s Planner–Coder–Critic pipeline in the supplied implementation.

appendix_entries.title: TeachQuiz equations and prompts
appendix_entries.body: TeachQuiz uses Eq. 1 for post-video quiz correctness and Eq. 2 to subtract an unlearned baseline. Eq. 3 and Eq. 4 are grounded in stage5_unlearning.py prompts that require NULL or insufficient evidence when knowledge is not available from the allowed source.

appendix_entries.title: Main results in Table 1
appendix_entries.body: Table 1 compares human-crafted videos, pixel-based models, direct Code LLM generation, agentic generation, and Code2Video variants using efficiency, aesthetics dimensions, AES Avg, and Quiz. The section text reports Code2Video improves AES and TeachQuiz over pixel and direct-code baselines.

appendix_entries.title: Quality and efficiency ablations
appendix_entries.body: Table 2 removes Planner, External Database, Visual Anchor, and Critic to test quality components. Table 3 removes parallel execution and ScopeRefine to test scalability. Table 7 varies visual-anchor granularity and reports the 6×6 grid as the best trade-off in AES Avg.

appendix_entries.title: Human study and TeachQuiz validity
appendix_entries.body: Table 4 asks whether human ratings align with automated trends across aesthetics, TeachQuiz, completion willingness, and ranking. Table 5 tests evidence sources for TeachQuiz, separating full video learning from text-only, animation-only, and random-video alternatives.

appendix_entries.title: Evidence versus open questions
appendix_entries.body: Table 1 supports reported gains in AES Avg and TeachQuiz for Code2Video variants. The open questions are not the same claim: Eq. 1–2 scoring is only candidate-grounded in the supplied repository artifacts, and the paper’s conclusion still names future work.

appendix_entries.title: Future work on scope and scalability
appendix_entries.body: The paper’s conclusion states that future work includes broadening the video scope and developing more lightweight, scalable agent frameworks. This limits the conclusion to demonstrated gains, not universal coverage or final scalability.

manim_compatibility.statement: The formula primitives have observed render evidence on Manim 0.19.0 and 0.20.1. No minimum-version compatibility claim is made.
